newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico electric restructuring stalls on divestiture.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico electric restructuring stalls on divestiture.

text.p: The collaborative effort to draft electric industry restructuring legislation in New Mexico reached an impasse Tuesday on the subject who should control power generation, according to Public Service Co of New Mexico.

PNM said it and the other regulated utilities found unacceptable a demand that they either lease or divest their electric distribution systems to an independent operator or divest their generation and energy services businesses.
A number of consumer groups rejected a proposal made by PNM late last week and found a second proposal offered by Southwestern Public Service Co Monday also unacceptable.

PNM spokeswoman Barbara Barsky said the company proposed retail wheeling start in January 2001 and that it be allowed to collect the cost of nuclear power through a wire charge over the period of its leases on those plants which end in 2016.

The utility will also reduce rates $10 million per year immediatly, or speed depreciation by that amount until 2001 to mitigate stranded costs and said it would take the risk on its oil, gas and coal generated power, she said.
A Southwestern PS spokesman said details on the company's offer would be available later today.
Other utilities operating in the state are El Paso Electric Co and TNP Enterprises Inc.

In its May 6 order approving a collaborative process, the New Mexico Public Utility Commission specified that, if the talks end prior to consensus, PNM would be required to make an electric rate filing within 30 days, it noted.

The company intends to continue discussions with those customers and other interested parties still committed to finding a workable restructuring approach for consideration by the New Mexico Legislature in January 1998.

In addition, the collaborative facilitators have indicated they would file a report with the commission reviewing the process followed, identifying future options and suggesting alternative approaches to reaching agreement on the conditions of restructuring in New Mexico.
